result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [check()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | whittaker description: Produce GAM diagnostic plots. twitter-card: title: >- [check()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | whittaker description: Produce GAM diagnostic plots. title: >- [check()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Produce GAM diagnostic plots. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Produce GAM diagnostic plots. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/plotting.py#L380-L558){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature check( model, plots=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Provides the standard suite of residual diagnostics used to assess GAM fit quality, analogous to `mgcv::gam.check()` in R. All requested diagnostics are returned as a single vertically concatenated Altair chart so calling `wk.check(model)` as the last expression in a cell displays inline. Available plots (selected via `plots=`): - `"qq"`: QQ plot of deviance residuals against theoretical normal quantiles. Systematic curvature away from the reference line suggests the response distribution (family) may be misspecified. - `"residuals"`: Pearson residuals vs fitted values. A even, patternless scatter around zero is the target; funnel shapes suggest heteroscedasticity (consider a location-scale family), and curvature suggests a missing or under-smoothed term. - `"histogram"`: Histogram of deviance residuals, for checking overall symmetry and shape. - `"response"`: Observed response vs fitted values, with a 1:1 reference line, for an overall sense of fit quality and to spot outliers. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [model]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [GAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A fitted GAM. [plots]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...] | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which diagnostic plots to include. Pass a list of names (e.g., `["qq", "residuals"]`) or `None` (default) for all four, in the order `"qq"`, `"residuals"`, `"histogram"`, `"response"`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [altair.VConcatChart]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : All requested diagnostic plots stacked vertically into a single chart. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#cfd8c76b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.gam import GAM from whittaker.plotting import check rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n) y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + rng.normal(scale=0.2, size=n) model = GAM("y ~ s(x)").fit({"x": x, "y": y}) chart = check(model, plots=["qq", "residuals"]) print(type(chart).__name__) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` VConcatChart ``` ::: :::
